text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today despite a backdrop of escalating Middle East tensions that have been pushing oil prices higher over the past two days. The stock had surged 11% in two weeks on mounting concerns about supply disruptions from Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi facilities, but today's small decline suggests those gains may have peaked as traders digested the actual impact: U.S. crude oil sits at $96 per barrel, still well above where it was two weeks ago, but the immediate threat assessment appears to have stabilized.

The divergence between U.S. and global oil prices—with Brent crude at $125 versus WTI at $96—reflects that most of the disruption risk remains in overseas shipping lanes rather than direct U.S. supply cuts. With the stock already up sharply on geopolitical premium, today's pullback is a natural pause in a volatile rally rather than a sign of deteriorating fundamentals for a major oil producer.
